description: Our team is excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are committed to working together, sharing ideas, learning new skills, and developing an innovative solution to the selected problem. Every team member will contribute their knowledge and creativity to complete the project successfully. We aim to learn from this experience and create something meaningful using science and technology.
summary: COSMIC EYE – NASA Space Discovery Explorer is a web-based application designed to help users explore the universe and learn about astronomical discoveries. The application provides an interactive platform with a modern, dark space-themed interface. It includes different sections such as Home, Explorer, Image Lab, Planet Nine, and Dashboard. The Explorer section helps users discover information about planets, stars, and galaxies. The Image Lab focuses on viewing and comparing astronomical images. The Planet Nine section provides information about the possible existence of an undiscovered planet in our solar system. The Dashboard presents astronomy-related information and observations. The application aims to make space exploration more interesting, accessible, and understandable through an interactive user interface. It is developed as a web application using modern web technologies and is designed to work on both desktop and mobile devices. Overall, COSMIC EYE encourages curiosity and provides an engaging way to explore space science and astronomical information.
details: Cosmic Eye is a web-based space exploration platform developed by Team HackHive for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It uses NASA SPHEREx astronomical observations to help users explore different regions of the sky and understand the universe. The platform allows users to view astronomical images, compare observations captured at different times, and explore possible changes in celestial object positions. It uses React.js, Python, FastAPI, OpenCV, NumPy, and SQLite. The main aim is to simplify complex space data through a user-friendly interface, making astronomy more accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
